newsitem.title: UK: Novartis overtakes Glaxo as biggest drug firm.
newsitem.headline: Novartis overtakes Glaxo as biggest drug firm.

text.p: Newly-created Swiss pharmaceuticals giant Novartis AG has knocked Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc off its perch as the world's biggest drugs company in terms of sales, information group IMS said on Friday.

IMS said that although both companies had a 4.4 percent share of global drug sales in 1996, Novartis was just ahead in total sales terms. Novartis was formed last year through the agreed merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz.

Glaxo Wellcome, also created through merger in 1995, faces a further challenge to its dominance this year when its top-selling drug Zantac loses its key U.S. patent, which is expected to lead to a rash of generic competitors.
The creation of Novartis pushed U.S. group Merck & Co into third place from second with a 4.0 percent market share.

But IMS said while both Glaxo Wellcome and Novartis saw a drop in market share compared with 1994, Merck's share had risen from 3.4 percent over the same period. It said Merck had achieved growth through a different strategy, "namely joint ventures and alliances and new product development."

IMS said another company formed by merger in 1995, German Hoechst AG's subsidiary Hoechst Marion Roussell, also saw its market share slip last year to 3.3 percent from 3.5 percent in 1995 and 3.8 percent in 1994, putting it in fourth place overall.

The alliance of Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc edged up to 17th last year from 18th with market share of 1.8 percent, while Swedish group Astra AB climbed to 12th place from 16th with world market share rising to 2.1 percent from 1.9 percent.
Astra is growing strongly on the back of its ulcer drug Losec, which IMS said had now overtaken Zantac as the world's top-selling drug.
